description.p: Nexe is a real-time communication platform built for streamers and gaming communities. Everything that usually needs an external bot is built in.

ul.li: Servers with channels, roles and permissions
Text chat with threads, reactions and search
Native Twitch integration: live status, roles and clips

description.p: On Linux you can now share your screen in calls, with the quality your plan allows.
On Linux you can now see other people's cameras and shared screens in calls.
The DeepFilterNet noise suppression option is now available on every platform, not only in Linux voice calls.
Linux voice calls now use Nexe's own audio engine: per-user volume, working echo cancellation and a new AI noise suppression option (DeepFilterNet) in Voice & Video settings.
On Linux the window now has Nexe's own dark title bar with working minimize, maximize and close buttons, instead of the white system one.
New microphone test in Voice & Video settings: a live level meter and a button to hear yourself with your current settings. On Linux the device list now shows your real microphones and speakers.
Fix: the Linux release build installs the compiler the voice engine requires without prompts.
Fix: the Linux release build now uses the compiler the voice engine requires.
Voice calls on Linux now run on a native voice engine, because the web view used on Linux has no WebRTC. Audio first; camera and screen sharing follow.
Version bump to validate that Nexe reopens by itself after an update.
Fix: the restart after an update now starts Nexe by its full path, so it reopens on systems where the command is not found.
Version bump to validate that Nexe reopens by itself after an update.
Fix: if the system does not start the new version after an update, Nexe now asks the desktop to open it, and records why.
Version bump to validate that Nexe reopens by itself after an update.
Fix: Nexe now waits for the new version to start before closing itself after an update, so it reopens on its own.
Startup check now measures how the system launches a new Nexe after an update, to fix machines where it does not reopen.
Restart after an update now records more detail, and a short startup check helps diagnose machines where Nexe does not reopen.
Version bump to collect the restart report from an update.
After an update, Nexe now records how the restart went so a failed reopen can be diagnosed.
Version bump to validate that Nexe reopens by itself after an update.
More reliable restart after an update, and a clear message while waiting for the update permission.
Version bump to validate that Nexe updates itself on startup.
Nexe now installs new versions by itself when it starts, like on Windows.
Version bump to validate automatic updates on every platform.
Version bump to validate updating and restarting from the in-app notice.
Fix: the in-app update notice could be missed when the update was found during startup.
Version bump to validate the in-app update notice.
Nexe now checks for new versions by itself every few minutes and can update from the in-app notice.
Version bump to validate in-app Flatpak updates.
In-app updates for the Flatpak build: Nexe now tells you when a new version is available and can update and restart itself.
Flatpak packaging for Linux, with updates delivered through Flatpak.
Linux fixes, Twitch device-code login and improved voice and video.
